description: Issue #839 AC1: `define foo` twice is an ERROR, not a silent override. Phase-1 registration raises `ol-duplicate-definition` carrying BOTH spans — `source_span` at the later declaration, `params.original_span` at the earlier one (`spec/error-model.md:126,143-146`) — and `spec/execution-model.md:86-88` makes it "MUST NOT be a silent override". The two bodies print DIFFERENT values on purpose, so the fixture discriminates between all three candidate rules — last-wins prints `222`, first-wins prints `111`, and only the ruling's rule produces the empty event stream asserted here. The `foo` call on line 7 is likewise deliberate: it proves nothing runs at all, rather than merely that the definitions were rejected. Core Language only, because phase-1 registration is unconditional — no profile decides whether a program may declare a name.
